implement.approach: Started from BASE_SHA on devin/pp/w02-03/impl-r3. Ported the sound r2 harness (child Node process + node:sqlite, 12 deterministic kill points via a kill switch armed by PD_KILL/PD_KILL_ID, loopback rating service with idempotent reserve/finalize/shots:sync). Added a fault-injecting loopback proxy (faultProxy.ts: 200 text/html, 204 empty, 301/302/307/308 -> captive-portal HTML or JSON 404 route, stall) and `runLaunches()` multi-launch orchestration so the suite can drive kill -> faulted relaunch -> honest relaunch sequences. Regression tests committed FIRST (dc3055f1; 10 failed on that commit: 9 shipping-path + 1 hermeticity). In-scope fix committed separately (1e9eedb9): harness.ts spawns children with every inherited PD_* variable stripped, so ambient PD_KILL never arms a launch. The shipping-path fix (out of scope for W02-03, on the side branch 46ad4433) changes only api.ts: (1) request() throws ApiError(502,'network.redirected') when `response.redirected` or `response.url` differs from the requested URL, so every call site (release, syncShots, ...) classifies redirected answers as transient — this alone makes the shot-sync redirect->404 cases retryable with attempts 0, no sync.ts change needed; (2) release() requires the 2xx acknowledgement to be a JSON object and, when it names a permit, that it is this permit, not `reserved`, and not settled as another outcome; otherwise ApiError(502,'access.permit_release_unconfirmed') so runJournal keeps the attempt `release_pending` under the same permit id. Rule kept tolerant of bodies without a `permit` key ({}, {ok:true}) because 13 existing test fakes (704 tests) answer finalize that way and tests may not be modified.

residual_risks: Linux/Node harness only (Node 24.19.0, node:sqlite, undici fetch): it does not establish native iOS runtime behaviour. The redirect detection relies on `Response.redirected`/`Response.url`; INFERRED (not verified on device) that React Native's whatwg-fetch populates `url` from XHR `responseURL` after NSURLSession follows a redirect.

The finalize acknowledgement rule accepts any JSON object without a `permit` key (e.g. `{}`) as a verdict, to stay compatible with 13 existing test fakes that cannot be modified under this package; a hostile intermediary returning JSON `{}` with 200 would still be recorded as released. The production route always answers `{permit, access}`, so a stricter `permit`-required check is possible once those fakes are updated (out of W02-03 scope).

Kill points are deterministic instrumentation points inside the harness child (SQLite statement hooks + fetch hooks), not OS-level random SIGKILL timing; 12 points cover every journal/result/outbox step but not arbitrary instruction boundaries.
